research_attempts.query_text: Inovar A Wallace; NARA OSS index context; CIA Reading Room exact-name domain check; Library of Congress exact-name collection check; exact-name and meaningful variants; OSS, rank, branch, identifier and assignment clues; employer and occupation 1940; obituary, institutional, newspaper, directory and archival searches; indexed Box 812, 813 or 814; protected identifiers used only in private official-record comparison
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Unbridged namesakes, snippets, commercial people-finder pages, relatives, unsourced genealogy, postwar-only leads, and sources without an OSS, protected-identifier, rank, unit, or personnel-file bridge were rejected. The Henry A. Wallace family lead, Paul Kimball Wallace obituary, and Helen Wallin alumni-page lead were not assigned without a direct bridge. Historical occupations were not converted into named employers, and the post-OSS Inovar/Ingvar Army occupation was withheld from pre-OSS claims.
research_attempts.research_notes: The protected-identifier Inovar/Ingvar bridge was accepted at high confidence, but its November 1945 Army entry cannot establish pre-OSS occupation. Exact-name OSS, employer, occupation, obituary, institutional, newspaper, official-domain, and archival searches were checked as applicable. Grouped CIA Reading Room and Library of Congress discovery checks produced no additional publishable employer source for the cohort. The NARA index page was text-extracted, rendered, and visually checked; official Army bulk data, technical documentation, and code documentation were inspected locally. The CIA Waller release and Phi Kappa Psi obituary were opened and visually inspected. No search-result snippet was used as sole final evidence, no paywall or access control was bypassed, and no authenticated NARA Catalog API call was made.
research_attempts.next_action: Review the indexed personnel file for corroborating identifiers, the immediate pre-OSS affiliation, and the last civilian employer before wartime service.
